stem: The causality behind the sudden changes was understood due to ____________ principle of Hugo de Vries.
solution: Hugo de Vries proposed the Mutation theory. According to it, sudden, large, inheritable changes (mutations) in organisms are responsible for the sudden appearance of new characters and new species. Hence the correct alternative is (B) Mutation.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: After complete oxidation of a glucose molecule, ____________ number of ATP molecules are formed.
solution: Complete (aerobic) oxidation of one glucose molecule yields a net total of 38 ATP molecules (glycolysis + Krebs cycle + electron transport chain). Hence the correct alternative is (C) 38.

stem: Bat is included in class ____________.
solution: A bat is a flying mammal. It has mammary glands, body hair and gives birth to young ones, so it belongs to class Mammalia (not Aves, even though it can fly). Hence the correct alternative is (D) Mammalia.

stem: In Maharashtra the major hydroelectric power plant is located at ____________.
solution: The Koyna (Koyana) Hydroelectric Project on the river Koyna is the largest hydroelectric power plant in Maharashtra. (Chandrapur and Parali are thermal plants; Tarapur is a nuclear plant.) Hence the correct alternative is (B) Koyana.

stem: A first state to start a separate cyber crime unit in our country is ____________.
solution: Maharashtra was the first state in India to start a separate cyber crime unit (cyber police stations) to deal with cyber crimes. Hence the correct alternative is (B) Maharashtra.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Complete the following activity by filling the box with the proper word. Asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms takes place by: Binary fission, Multiple fission and ____________.
solution: The third type is Budding. Asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms takes place by Binary fission (e.g. Amoeba), Multiple fission (e.g. Plasmodium) and Budding (e.g. yeast).

stem: Which day is observed as World Biodiversity Day?
solution: 22nd May is observed as World Biodiversity Day (International Day for Biological Diversity).

stem: Identify me, who am I? I was the first clone sheep born in Scotland.
solution: Dolly. Dolly the sheep was the first cloned mammal (clone sheep), produced by the Roslin Institute in Scotland in 1996.

stem: Write the molecular formula of acetic acid.
solution: The molecular formula of acetic acid is \(CH_3COOH\), i.e. \(C_2H_4O_2\). (Acetic acid / vinegar is produced industrially by the bacterium Acetobacter aceti during fermentation.)
figureNote: Chemistry-crossover recall item appearing in the Biology paper; chapter assignment (Introduction to Microbiology, acetic-acid fermentation) is a best-fit and may need review.

stem: State whether the following statement is true or false: The chairman of National Disaster Management is Sarpanch.
solution: False. The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio chairman of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), not the Sarpanch.

stem: Give scientific reason: The popularity of probiotic products is increasing.
solution: Probiotic products (like certain yoghurts and fermented milk) contain beneficial live microorganisms such as Lactobacillus. These microbes maintain and restore the useful microflora of the intestine, help in digestion, improve absorption of nutrients, increase immunity and protect against harmful microbes (especially after a course of antibiotics). Because of these health benefits, the popularity of probiotic products is increasing.

stem: Give scientific reason: Body temperature of reptiles is not constant.
solution: Reptiles are cold-blooded (poikilothermic / ectothermic) animals. They do not possess an efficient internal mechanism to regulate and maintain a constant body temperature. Therefore their body temperature changes with the temperature of the surrounding environment, i.e. it is not constant.

stem: Give scientific reason: Nowadays farmers are opting for organic farming.
solution: In organic farming, chemical fertilizers and chemical pesticides are avoided and biofertilizers (e.g. Rhizobium, Azotobacter) and biopesticides are used instead. This keeps the soil fertile and its useful microflora intact, avoids pollution of soil and water, produces chemical-residue-free (safe) food and is eco-friendly. Because it protects health and the environment while maintaining soil fertility, farmers nowadays are opting for organic farming.

stem: What is meant by carbon dating? Give any one use of this technique.
solution: Carbon dating is a technique used to determine the age of fossils and ancient organic remains by measuring the amount of the radioactive isotope carbon-14 (\(C^{14}\)) still present in them. Use: It is used to estimate the age of fossils, which provides evidence for the study of evolution (also used to date archaeological objects).

context: Read the paragraph and answer the questions: Paddy is cultivated on large scale in various states of South India. Paddy fields are frequently attacked by grasshoppers. Similarly, frogs are also present in large number in the mud of paddy fields, to feed upon grasshoppers, and snakes are also present therein to feed upon their favourite food - frogs. However, if frog population declines all of a sudden,
stem: What will be the effect on paddy crop?
solution: If the frog population declines suddenly, the grasshoppers (which the frogs used to eat) are no longer controlled and their number increases greatly. These grasshoppers feed on the paddy plants, so the paddy crop will be badly damaged and its yield will decrease (the crop may be destroyed).

context: Read the paragraph and answer the questions: Paddy is cultivated on large scale in various states of South India. Paddy fields are frequently attacked by grasshoppers. Similarly, frogs are also present in large number in the mud of paddy fields, to feed upon grasshoppers, and snakes are also present therein to feed upon their favourite food - frogs. However, if frog population declines all of a sudden,
stem: Number of which components will increase?
solution: The number of grasshoppers will increase, because their predator (the frog) has declined and no longer controls them. (At the same time the number of snakes will decrease, as they lose their food, the frogs.)

stem: Write any two advantages of hydroelectric power generation.
solution: Any two advantages of hydroelectric power generation: (1) It uses flowing/stored water, which is a renewable and clean source, so there is no air pollution and no fuel cost. (2) The same water can be used again for irrigation and drinking, and the dam also helps in flood control; the running cost is low and power generation is continuous.

stem: The following are the pictures of some disasters. How will your post-disaster management be, in case you face any of those disasters? (A) Gas / chemical leak  (B) Storm / flood.
solution: (A) Gas / chemical leak: Cover the nose and mouth with a wet cloth, move quickly to an open area against the wind, evacuate people from the affected zone, give first aid and shift the affected to hospital, and immediately inform the fire brigade and disaster-control authorities. (B) Storm / flood: Shift people and animals to safe higher places or relief camps, provide clean drinking water, food and medicines, give first aid, help in rescue and rehabilitation, and restore essential services once the disaster is over.
figureNote: Two disaster pictures on p-04: (A) a person covering face near a leaking gas cylinder (gas/chemical leak) and (B) a house in heavy storm/flood.

stem: Explain the theory of Lamarckism with the help of any two suitable examples.
solution: Lamarckism (theory of inheritance of acquired characters) was proposed by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck. It states that (a) organs that are used more become well developed and organs that are not used degenerate (use and disuse of organs), and (b) such characters acquired during the lifetime of an organism are inherited by the next generation, leading to evolution. Examples: (1) Giraffe - its ancestors had short necks; by constantly stretching to reach leaves on tall trees the neck became longer, and this long neck was passed on to the offspring. (2) Snakes / limbless animals - due to their burrowing and creeping habit the limbs were not used and gradually disappeared (disuse of organs); the limbless condition was inherited.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Name the type of cells in which mitosis occurs. Write the four stages of karyokinesis.
solution: Mitosis occurs in somatic cells (body cells / vegetative cells). The four stages of karyokinesis (division of the nucleus) are: (1) Prophase, (2) Metaphase, (3) Anaphase and (4) Telophase.

stem: Give two examples of each of the threatened species given below: (a) Endangered species  (b) Rare species  (c) Vulnerable species.
solution: (a) Endangered species: Tiger and Great Indian Bustard (also Asiatic lion, Blackbuck). (b) Rare species: Indian wild ass and Red panda (also Great Indian hornbill). (c) Vulnerable species: Gaur (Indian bison) and Sloth bear. [These are threatened categories of biodiversity that need conservation.]

stem: Which fuel is used in a thermal power plant? What are the problems associated with this type of power generation?
solution: A thermal power plant mainly uses coal as the fuel (natural gas or diesel may also be used). Problems associated with it: (1) Coal is a non-renewable fossil fuel whose reserves are limited and getting exhausted. (2) Burning of coal releases large amounts of \(CO_2\), \(SO_2\), smoke and fly-ash, causing air pollution, acid rain and the greenhouse effect (global warming). (3) A large quantity of ash is produced, which needs disposal and pollutes land and water.

stem: Identify the type of body symmetry of the animals shown in the given pictures (A), (B) and (C).
solution: (A) Asymmetry (asymmetrical body, e.g. Amoeba / sponge - the body cannot be divided into equal halves by any plane). (B) Radial symmetry (the body can be divided into equal halves by any plane passing through the central axis, e.g. jellyfish / Hydra / starfish). (C) Bilateral symmetry (the body can be divided into two equal right and left halves by only one plane, e.g. the quadruped animal shown, like a goat/dog).
figureNote: Three animal pictures on p-05 labelled (A), (B), (C) illustrating body symmetry (A asymmetrical blob, B radially symmetrical animal, C a bilaterally symmetrical quadruped).

stem: Complete the following conceptual picture with respect to the uses of Xanthan gum (fill the six boxes surrounding 'Xanthan gum').
solution: Xanthan gum (a microbial polysaccharide produced by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris) has the following uses: (1) as a thickening agent in the food industry (sauces, soups, ice creams), (2) as a stabilizer and emulsifier in food products, (3) in the pharmaceutical industry (syrups and medicines), (4) in cosmetics (creams, lotions, toothpaste), (5) in the petroleum/oil-drilling industry (drilling fluids), and (6) in the paint and textile industry (as a gelling/binding agent).

stem: Which precautions will you take during the spraying of pesticides?
solution: Precautions during spraying of pesticides: (1) Wear protective clothing, gloves, goggles and a mask, and cover the nose and mouth. (2) Always spray in the direction of the wind (keep the wind at your back) so that the spray does not blow onto you. (3) Do not eat, drink or smoke while spraying. (4) Keep children, other people and food/water sources away from the spraying area. (5) After spraying, wash the hands, body and clothes thoroughly, and store the pesticides safely away from food and out of reach of children.

stem: Write the names of any six materials in a first aid box.
solution: Any six materials found in a first aid box: (1) Antiseptic solution (e.g. Dettol / Savlon), (2) Tincture iodine or antiseptic cream, (3) Sterile cotton, (4) Bandage / gauze, (5) Adhesive tape / band-aid (adhesive dressing), and (6) Scissors. (Others: thermometer, ORS packet, pain-relief balm, safety pins, disposable gloves.)

stem: Write the names of any six factors affecting social health.
solution: Any six factors affecting social health: (1) Unemployment, (2) Poverty, (3) Addiction (alcohol, tobacco, drugs), (4) Illiteracy / lack of education, (5) Superstitions and blind faith, and (6) Crime and terrorism. (Others: corruption, population explosion, gender inequality, misuse of social media / cyber crime.)

stem: What will you do? Why? Your brother studying in XII has developed stress.
solution: What I will do: I will talk to him calmly and listen to his problems patiently, help him plan his studies with a proper time-table and short breaks, encourage him to do regular exercise, yoga, meditation and pursue a hobby, ensure he gets adequate sleep and a balanced diet, and if the stress is severe, seek the help of parents/teachers or a counsellor. Why: Unmanaged stress harms both mental and physical health and reduces concentration and performance. Timely support and relaxation techniques help him overcome the stress, regain confidence and study/perform better.
